items.name: Sable
items.description: IGN "Sable", blue-side jungler on Rengar. Builds pure damage — lethality, crit, armor penetration, no defensive item — so one combo either erases a squishy or leaves him dead. Twelve-year-old mouse with a chipped button, instant coffee between games, a jaw that clicks when he is calculating. Speaks in timers and short calls; treats every fight as a clock he has to beat.
invariants: Full-damage build only; Sable never buys defensive items.
Sable plays Rengar this game.

items.name: Bram
items.description: Top laner on Ornn. A man in his forties with a smoker going in the yard; discusses brisket temperatures and his lawn while last-hitting, counts minions out loud, and says "we scale" every time the team is behind. Slow, calm, immovable voice. Never tilts, never types in all chat, and quietly takes every side lane nobody else will look at.
invariants: Bram never tilts and never forfeits.
Bram's champion is Ornn.

items.name: Priya
items.description: Mid laner on Viktor, a nursing student on night shifts. Her building's power cut at 12:00 and her client dropped; she is gone exactly fifteen minutes and comes back at 27:00 apologizing in caps. Speaks in hospital metaphors — triage, vitals, code blue. Wants a surrender vote when she returns, then becomes the calmest voice on the team. Lives and dies by the gravity cage and the Death Ray.
invariants: Priya's disconnect lasts fifteen minutes of game clock.
Priya's champion is Viktor.

items.name: Bex
items.description: ADC on Sivir, playing on a laptop trackpad with a cat named Wonton walking over the keyboard. 0/7 before the comeback. Apologizes constantly in chat ("my b", "sorry sorry"), overextends for one extra minion, and still has the best hands on the team once the panic stops. Sivir's On the Hunt is blue's only speed button and the key to every winning push.
invariants: Bex is heavily behind before the comeback.
Bex plays on a trackpad with a cat wandering the desk.

items.name: Moth
items.description: Support on Lulu. Hyper-competitive teenager with a spreadsheet tracking enemy summoner-spell timers, called out to the second. Refuses to type "gg" before the nexus actually falls, keeps a lucky coin balanced on the monitor, takes one loud breath before every objective, and hates a wasted spell more than a lost fight.
invariants: Moth never forfeits and never types "gg" early.
Moth's champion is Lulu.

items.name: Summoner's Rift, night queue
items.description: Three lanes and two rivers, a Baron pit that opens at 20:00, Elder Dragon territory beyond. Blue base has two nexus turrets standing behind its inhibitors; red base mirrors it. Fog of war decides most fights: one missing ward turns a clean push into a slaughter, and the width of the lane mouth is the difference between a siege and a death trap.
invariants: Three lanes, inhibitors, and two nexus turrets per base.

items.name: Match economics and clock
items.description: Kills, assists, towers, inhibitors and neutral monsters all pay gold; bounties grow on a streak, so the losing team can harvest a fortune from one fed enemy. Baron Nashor appears at 20:00 and grants a team-wide buff plus empowered minions. A destroyed inhibitor pumps super minions down that lane until it rebuilds. The clock runs in minutes and seconds and is the spine of every decision in the story.
invariants: Timers are quoted as mm:ss and stay consistent.
Baron buff empowers minions and hands the pushing team the initiative.

items.name: Full-damage Rengar
items.description: Lethality and crit with no defensive item, so the engage window is one leap. Thrill of the Hunt reveals the nearest enemy and lets Sable leap from camouflage with bonus ferocity; a full-ferocity combo deletes a squishy in under a second. If the combo misses, or a shield or spell shield eats it, Sable dies almost instantly. Every ult is a single-use key, never a sustained fight.
invariants: Each ult creates one kill window and offers no second chance.
Sable dies when his engage is spoiled.

items.name: Red team and its late-game ceiling
items.description: Red: Renekton top, Lee Sin jungle, Talon mid, Draven ADC, Pyke support. Their win condition is picks and Baron pressure in the first half. Late they have no reliable ranged waveclear, every engage tool is single-target (kick, hook, dash), and shields or a spell shield spoil the combo. Renekton's damage falls off, Draven must catch axes to keep his, Pyke's resets need kills that stop coming, and Talon cannot leave after a dive. They cannot siege a grouped base.
invariants: Red's engage tools are single-target only.
Red has no sustained ranged waveclear for super minions.

items.name: The comeback line
items.description: Blue loses a Baron fight, gives up an inhibitor, and defends three super-minion sieges. Each Rengar ult converts into one kill and one objective, and the gap closes on bounties and picks rather than on a single miracle fight. The arc ends with a backdoored second inhibitor and a push under the nexus turrets.

items.name: Sable's seat
items.description: First person, past tense, from the jungler's chair: the reader only sees what Sable's screen, his team's comms and his map awareness allow. Timers, gold counts and respawn clocks are used as beats, and every teammate is characterized through the voice coming down the voice chat.

items.name: Bex and Moth, lane partners
items.description: Moth tracks Bex's summoner spells and calls his overextensions a half second before they happen; Bex apologizes and does it anyway. Their trust is rebuilt during the super-minion sieges, when a landed spell shield matters more than any apology.

chapters.title: Ten Seconds of Gray Screen
points: Sable respawns at 26:12 into a base under Baron buff: 6–19 on kills, nine thousand gold behind, Priya's client dark since 12:00.
Bram counts minions out loud while tanking at the tier-two tower; Moth rattles off timers; Bex apologizes for his seventh death.
First ult: Draven steps past his own ward to catch an axe at the river mouth, and Sable deletes him in one leap.
The Baron push stalls, but Renekton and Lee Sin crack the mid inhibitor before the wave breaks — super minions are coming.

chapters.title: Fifteen Minutes
points: Wave one of super minions hits mid and the team discovers how little waveclear it has without Viktor.
Priya reconnects at 27:00 in caps, apologizing, and immediately asks for a surrender vote; Moth refuses to type gg.
Sable's second ult picks Pyke at the inhibitor; the wave breaks with the nexus untouched but two turrets bleeding.
Priya's cage buys the first clean disengage and the team settles on Bram's mantra: we scale.

chapters.title: Wave Two
points: Red returns with a fresh Baron buff and a second super wave; Talon's dive dies on Ornn's knockup.
Sable trades his own life for Draven and Lee Sin, and the gold gap shrinks to four thousand on bounties.
Red's flaws surface under pressure: single-target engage, no ranged waveclear while grouped, Renekton's fury spent on minions.
Red takes another Baron at 32:00 while the third super wave forms, and the base braces for the worst of it.

chapters.title: The Third Wave
points: The hardest siege: super minions and Baron buff in mid, a sideline wave climbing top.
Bex lands the spell shield that eats Pyke's hook and clears a wave without dying; Moth's calls go quiet and exact.
Sable's fourth ult kills Draven beside his own nexus turret and the wave finally dies at the turrets.
The base holds with the nexus exposed, and the team decides to step outside.

chapters.title: Out
points: Blue pushes out on three lanes, wins the river fight, and secures Baron at 35:40.
Priya's cage splits Red at the pit; Bram walks a super wave down mid alone, counting it.
With the buff, blue takes top tier two and the top inhibitor — the first one — and Red's nexus turrets come live.
Red respawns and blue backs off with seconds of Baron still ticking.

chapters.title: Their Late Game
points: Blue converts the Baron into mid tier two and two picks; Red turtles behind its nexus turrets.
Red's late-game ceiling shows: Renekton's damage gone, Draven's axes caught by nobody, Talon stranded after his dive.
A straight five-on-five siege costs blue three lives for nothing, and Sable admits the turrets cannot be cracked head-on.
Priya offers the alternative: bait Baron, and let Sable take the second inhibitor alone.

chapters.title: The Second Inhibitor
points: Moth's script: four of blue show at Baron while Sable waits in red's bottom jungle behind a control ward.
Bex's On the Hunt sells the bait; Red takes it and rotates to the pit, Renekton's recall already spent.
Sable backdoors the bottom inhibitor with eight seconds of vision and a stopwatch in his ear.
The second inhibitor falls, two lanes turn into super minions, and Red's base begins dying from the inside.

chapters.title: Nexus Turrets
points: Blue walks in behind two super waves; the first nexus turret falls and Red's last stand begins.
Deaths trade both ways as Bex's speed button carries blue under the second turret and Moth lands every shield.
Sable's final ult erases Draven at the nexus while Priya's Death Ray cuts the wave behind them.
The nexus falls, the win screen arrives, and Moth types gg at last.

args.brief: Chapter 1, "Ten Seconds of Gray Screen." Open in the exact instant Sable's gray screen ends and the respawn animation starts at 26:12, right after blue lost the Baron fight. Establish the disaster: 6–19 kills, roughly nine thousand gold down, blue's mid inhibitor turret already dead, Baron buff on red, and Priya's client dark since 12:00 (fifteen minutes). Give each teammate a voice and a quirk in the voice chat: Bram's calm brisket-and-lawn monologue plus his minion counting while he tanks; Moth's stopwatch timers and refusal to forfeit; Bex apologizing for his seventh death while his cat walks the keyboard. Sable is full-damage Rengar, no defensive item, one combo or death. End the chapter on the first snowball ult: Draven steps past his pink ward at the river mouth to catch an axe, Sable leaps, kills him, and the Baron push stalls — but Renekton and Lee Sin crack blue's mid inhibitor before the wave breaks, so super minions are coming. Keep first person limited, match-clock beats, quick and hard-bitten voice. Roughly 1200 words.

Chapter 2, "Fifteen Minutes." Start at 28:15 with the first super-minion wave walking into blue's base on mid. Show the defense in detail: Bram's Ornn holds the lane mouth while counting the super minions aloud, Moth calls every timer and refuses to vote surrender, Bex's Sivir clears the wave but overextends and needs saving. Bring out Priya's return properly — she is calm, speaks in hospital metaphors, apologizes, and her Viktor is behind (level and items) but her gravity cage and Death Ray are the only real waveclear blue has. Let one red player (Rengar's counterpart, Lee Sin or the Draven) talk trash in all chat, and let the reader feel red's late-game weakness without naming it outright: they can only start fights one target at a time. Snowball beat: Sable's second ult kills Pyke near the inhibitor, and the wave breaks with the nexus untouched but a tier-two turret and a nexus turret damaged. End on the team's decision and Bram's mantra "we scale," and a hook that the second wave is already forming. First person, clock beats, roughly 1200 words.

Chapter 3, "Wave Two." Jump to about 29:45, the second super-minion push. Red still has no Baron buff (theirs expired), so they have to push with super minions and picks alone — show them trying the same single-key engage again and getting punished. Give each teammate a quirk beat: Bram counting the wave while quietly buying a defensive item and telling a brisket story that turns out to be about patience; Moth's stopwatch and the coin on his monitor, calling the enemy flashes exactly; Bex overextending again but landing a Ricochet that saves the wave; Priya triaging the fight like an ER and telling people who to let die. Snowball beat: Sable's third ult kills Draven, and he then trades his own life to take Lee Sin down too — the double kill plus shutdown gold closes the deficit to roughly four thousand. Make red's late-game ceiling explicit in Sable's analysis: Renekton's fury spent on minions, Pyke's resets dead, Talon can only go in once, Draven must catch axes to do damage. Then at 32:00 Baron spawns and red takes it while blue is still clearing — end the chapter with the third wave forming and red returning with the buff, and Moth saying the number. First person, clock beats, roughly 1200 words.

Chapter 4, "The Third Wave." This is the hardest siege: it starts around 33:00 with Baron-buffed super minions on mid plus a side wave climbing top, so blue has to split. Show real attrition — Bram's Ornn takes the brunt and his calm finally cracks for one line before he gets it back; Moth calls every cooldown and this time his calls are perfect and quiet; Bex lands the spell shield that eats Pyke's hook and clears a wave without dying, and Moth actually says something kind; Priya works the fight like an ER, naming who she can save. Let a red player taunt in all chat and let red's comp pay for its late-game weakness: Renekton's damage is gone, Talon goes in once and is stranded, Pyke resets never come, Lee Sin's kick is single-target, nobody can clear Baron-empowered super minions. Snowball beat: Sable's fourth ult kills Draven beside the enemy's own push, and blue kills the wave at the nexus turrets. The nexus turrets survive with almost no health, and the chapter ends with the team deciding to step outside rather than wait for a fourth wave. First person, clock beats, roughly 1200 words.

Chapter 5, "Out." Start around 34:20 with blue pushing out of its own base for the first time in ages — three lanes, ward line, Moth's countdown. Blue wins the river fight at 34:50 with Priya's cage splitting red and Bram's Ornn engage, and secures Baron at 35:40. Show the swing in the gold graph and the bounty math. Give each teammate a beat: Bram walks a super wave down mid alone and counts it out loud; Bex's On the Hunt is the first time her speed button matters; Moth calls the Baron pit like a surgeon; Priya directs traffic in hospital language and keeps her own Death Ray for the wave, not the champions. Snowball beat: Sable's fifth ult kills Talon before the Baron fight and his sixth ult kills Lee Sin at the pit. Then with the Baron buff blue takes top tier two and the top inhibitor — the FIRST inhibitor of the game for blue — and red's nexus turrets go live. End with red respawning, blue backing off with the buff still ticking, and the knowledge that now they have to do it again. First person, clock beats, roughly 1200 words.

Chapter 6, "Their Late Game." Around 37:20 to 40:00. Blue converts the remaining Baron window into mid tier two and two more picks, and red turtles behind its nexus turrets. Make red's late-game ceiling explicit and specific through Sable's analysis and the fight itself: Renekton's damage has evaporated, Draven must catch axes so he cannot kite backwards, Pyke's resets need kills red no longer gets, Talon can only enter once and cannot leave, Lee Sin's kick is a single-target tool against a team standing together — and none of them can clear a wave, so the super minions blue creates are permanent pressure. Then the failure: a straight five-on-five siege under red's nexus turrets costs blue three lives for nothing, and Sable admits the turrets cannot be cracked head-on while red is home. End with Priya proposing the alternative — bait Baron, and let Sable take the second inhibitor alone — and the team arguing about it before agreeing, with Moth's stopwatch and Bram's implicit trust. Bring out each teammate's quirk one more time before the plan: Bex apologizing and then committing, Moth refusing to vote gg, Bram counting. First person, clock beats, roughly 1200 words.

Chapter 7, "The Second Inhibitor." Start around 40:20 with the plan going live: four of blue show at the Baron pit at 41:20 while Sable waits in red's bottom-side jungle behind a control ward, with his ult at zero and his heart in his throat. Show the tension in the bait: Bex's On the Hunt carrying the four of blue into red's vision, Moth counting red's rotations to the second, Priya holding her cage for the exit instead of the entrance, Bram walking a super wave mid so red's base keeps bleeding. Renekton's recall is already spent, red takes the bait and rotates to the pit. Sable's backdoor against the second inhibitor — actually the mid inhibitor is the second one blue destroys; make it clear this is the second inhibitor of the game for blue. Show the turret hurting him, ferocity management, one ult used for the escape when Pyke comes back, the eight seconds of vision, and Moth's voice in his ear counting the enemy respawns. The inhibitor falls at a specific clock time. Then two lanes turn into super minions, and red's base starts dying from the inside. End on the four of blue disengaging from the pit alive and the team realizing they now only have to survive one push under the nexus turrets. First person, clock beats, roughly 1200 words.

Chapter 8, "Nexus Turrets." Final chapter, around 43:00 to the end. Blue walks in behind two super-minion waves (top and mid both open), with red pinned in its own base because they cannot clear supers and cannot leave. Build the tension of pushing under the nexus turrets in detail: the turret aggro order, Sable's full-damage body being one shot away from death, Moth calling the two turrets and every enemy cooldown to the second, Bram soaking aggro with Ornn and counting, Priya holding her Death Ray for the wave behind them and finally using it, Bex's On the Hunt carrying the team under the second turret, Bex landing the spell shield that eats Pyke's last hook. Red's comp breaks in exactly the way foreshadowed: Talon stranded, Renekton's damage gone, Lee Sin's single-target kick on a tank, Pyke's resets never coming, Draven caught out of position for an axe. Sable's final ult erases Draven at the nexus. Trade deaths, let someone die for real, then the last nexus turret falls and the nexus falls with Priya's Death Ray cutting the wave behind them rather than a champion. End on the win screen, the scoreboard showing the comeback, and Moth typing gg at last — small, quiet, earned — plus one closing beat from Bram counting. Keep it first person, clock beats, roughly 1200 words, and give the story a definite stopping point.

items.name: Dave
items.description: A man in his late thirties who has just moved into an old house with streaky windows. Practical, dryly funny, skeptical by habit, and quietly lonely in a way he would never say aloud. He notices small physical wrongnesses before he believes anything: a chair's angle, a cold seam in a hallway, dust patterns. He wants to be taken seriously by the person he loves, and he is ashamed of how much he wants it.
invariants: Sees ghosts in the house
Moves into the old house with streaky windows
Has a sensual encounter with one spirit

items.name: Mira
items.description: Dave's partner. Warm, quick, and fond of being the reasonable one; her teasing starts as affection and sharpens into a habit of scoring points. She does not see anything in the house and treats Dave's accounts as a bit he is doing for attention. She is not cruel by design, which makes the wedge worse: she keeps expecting him to laugh along.
invariants: Teases Dave about the ghosts
Does not see the ghosts

items.name: Hattie Vale
items.description: A spirit bound to the house, once a woman who kept its rooms and died there in the 1920s; her grave stands in the cemetery Dave walks past daily. She appears as cold air, the smell of camphor and rain, and a woman whose edges blur where the light is bad. She is courteous, formal, and starved for being addressed as a person rather than a phenomenon. She wants to be believed without being exposed.
invariants: Bound to the house and to her grave in the cemetery
Requires respect to be approached
Cannot be seen by Mira

items.name: The house on Larch Row
items.description: A narrow two-story house with a long dim hall, warped floorboards, and tall windows whose old glass is streaked in cloudy bands that smear the daylight into moving shapes. Rooms feel re-angled when Dave returns to them; furniture sits a few inches from where he left it. The hall is the spine of the haunting: cold, papered in faded green, lit by one weak bulb.
invariants: Windows remain streaked
Dim hallways
Furniture shifts on its own when unobserved

items.name: The misty cemetery
items.description: The burial ground on Dave's daily walk between the house and the rest of his life. Iron fence, gravel path, leaning stones, and morning mist that keeps its own weather. Hattie's stone is in the older row; the mist thickens there and the air smells of camphor. It is the one place where the haunting feels less like intrusion and more like an invitation.
invariants: Misty
Dave passes it every day

items.name: Respect is the hinge
items.description: The haunting answers to courtesy. Addressed plainly and without mockery, the dead can be met; mocked, filmed, tested, or talked over, they become colder, louder, and less careful with the living. Mira's teasing does not merely wound Dave; it teaches the house that he is not to be trusted with what he sees.
invariants: Contempt or ridicule sharpens and coarsens the manifestations
Plain acknowledgment allows contact

items.name: How the house shows itself
items.description: Furniture moves only when no one is looking, never in a witnessed instant. Shadow figures are fleeting, seen at the edge of vision or at the end of the hall, gone when looked at directly. Touch is possible only in low light and only when Dave is alone and calm; cold arrives first, then scent, then presence.
invariants: No witnessed instant of furniture movement
Shadow figures vanish when looked at directly

items.name: The wedge between Dave and Mira
items.description: The more Dave reports, the more Mira performs disbelief, and the more she performs it, the less he tells her. Their old intimacy of shared jokes turns into a power struggle over who gets to define what is real in their own home.
invariants: Teasing escalates rather than resolves
Dave withholds more as Mira teases more

items.name: Between disbelief and desire
items.description: Dave's sensual encounter with Hattie splits him: part of him insists it was cold, draft, grief, and a lonely man's imagination; the rest of him remembers being wanted by someone who saw him clearly. He cannot confess it to Mira without confirming every joke she has made.
invariants: Dave stays torn between disbelief and desire
The encounter cannot be easily explained away for him

items.name: Narration
items.description: Third person limited, past tense, anchored in Dave's senses and misgivings; literary, restrained, with concrete physical detail carrying the dread and the erotic charge. Scenes in the house stay close and low-lit; cemetery scenes are slower and mist-softened.
invariants: Third person limited to Dave
Past tense

items.name: Dave and Mira
items.description: Long-term partners who still love each other and have stopped listening in the same register. Affectionate on the surface, thinning underneath, with Mira holding the upper hand in any argument about what is real.

items.name: Dave and Hattie
items.description: Host and guest, then witness and witnessed, then something neither of them has a word for. Courtesy on both sides; want on both sides; the imbalance of living and dead always in the room.

args.viewpoint: Third person limited, anchored in Dave
args.tone: Restrained literary dread, cold sensuality, dry tenderness; longing held in physical detail rather than confession

chapters.title: Streaked Light
points: Dave walks through the empty house on Larch Row with the keys still warm in his hand, cataloguing the streaked windows and the long dim hall.
He sets the furniture straight by eye and starts carrying boxes; Mira arrives warm and joking and immediately rearranges his arrangement.
Alone at dusk he notices a chair has turned to face the hall; he tells himself he moved it and hears a floorboard take weight behind him.

chapters.title: The Reasonable One
points: Dave starts his daily walk past the misty cemetery and notices an old leaning stone in the front row; he begins to greet the house out of politeness, half joking.
Small wrongnesses multiply: drawer handles reversed, a lamp moved to the hall's end, a shadow figure crossing the doorway that is gone when he looks.
He tells Mira; she teases him in front of friends and films the hall theatrically, and the cold in the house sharpens in answer.
A door shuts hard enough to rattle the streaked glass, and Mira laughs it off while Dave stands in the cold seam of the hallway.

chapters.title: Camphor
points: Mira leaves for a work trip; alone for three nights, Dave stops mocking himself and speaks plainly to the empty hall.
The house answers with courtesy instead of pranks: warmth at the threshold, furniture set back the way he likes it, a smell of camphor and rain.
He sees Hattie properly for the first time at the end of the hall, blurred at the edges, and she asks him not to look away.
The chapter stops on the first touch of her cold hand and Dave's decision not to flinch.

chapters.title: The Long Hall
points: In the low light of the hall, Dave and Hattie's encounter becomes sensual, tender, and strange; he is wanted by someone who has watched him closely.
Afterward the house is quiet and the cold recedes; Dave lies awake cataloguing impossible details he cannot explain away.
By morning the hall is ordinary, the chair is where it always was, and doubt arrives with the daylight.
The chapter stops with Dave on the cemetery path, mist to his knees, unable to tell longing from grief.

chapters.title: Tests
points: Dave tries to prove the encounter was draft and grief: he seals the windows, marks the furniture with tape, and waits in the hall with a lamp all night.
The house refuses to perform for a test, and his doubts thicken; only when he apologizes for the tape does the hallway warm again.
Mira returns and the teasing resumes harder, now with an edge of hurt; Dave begins lying about what he sees to keep the peace.
The chapter stops with Dave in the cemetery at dusk, mist risen and a figure waiting between the stones that is not a shadow.

chapters.title: Her Name
points: In the mist Dave finds the leaning stone and reads the name Hattie Vale; the figure at the fence waits to be recognized rather than approached.
He tells Mira the truth about the grave, and she follows him there to be kind in the wrong way, mocking the stone and calling the whole thing a bit.
The mist turns hard and cold; something in the cemetery withdraws, and Mira finally feels it and is frightened rather than amused.
The chapter stops with Mira giving him a hard choice, and Dave staying behind in the fog with the name still in his mouth.

chapters.title: Respect
points: Dave tells Mira plainly, without joking or begging to be believed, what happened and what he wants; she cannot believe him but stops laughing for the first time.
He declines to make the house a battlefield: he corrects the chair's angle himself and says Hattie's name aloud in the hallway, on purpose.
Hattie answers once and does not stay to be studied; the wanting is mutual and the limit is acknowledged on both sides.
The house settles, Mira and Dave end in an honest, unresolved conversation at the door, and the story stops in the dim hall with the streaked window full of morning.

args.brief: Chapter 1. Open on the empty house on Larch Row: Dave with keys, catalogue the streaked tall windows smearing daylight, the long dim hall with its one weak bulb, the smell of old paper. Establish his dry humor and his practical habit of fixing small things — he squares the furniture by eye. Mira arrives warm, joking, and rearranges things; the first exchange of teasing, affectionate but with her holding the upper hand. End at dusk: the chair he set square now faces the hall, and a floorboard takes weight behind him. Keep third person limited past tense, concrete physical detail, no ghosts shown clearly yet.

Chapter 2, "The Reasonable One". Dave establishes his daily walk past the misty cemetery and notices an old leaning stone in the front row of graves; meanwhile the house's small wrongnesses multiply — drawer handles reversed, a lamp moved to the end of the hall, a shadow figure crossing the doorway that is gone when he looks directly. He tells Mira. Her teasing escalates: she performs disbelief in front of friends, films the hall theatrically, mocks the whole thing as his bit. Under the mockery the house turns colder, coarser — a drawer dumped, the lamp knocked over. End with a door shutting hard enough to rattle the streaked glass, Mira laughing it off, Dave standing in the cold seam of the hallway. Keep supernatural events unexplained-instantaneous: no witnessed furniture movement.

Chapter 3, "Camphor". Mira leaves for a work trip; Dave is alone in the house for three nights. He stops half-mocking himself and speaks plainly to the empty hall — greeting it, apologizing for the tape and the film-making. The house answers with courtesy rather than pranks: warmth at the threshold, furniture set back the way he likes it, a smell of camphor and rain arriving before anything visible. On the third night he sees Hattie properly at the end of the dim hall — a woman whose edges blur where the light is bad, formal, courteous, starved for being addressed as a person. She asks him not to look away and not to film her; he puts the phone down. End the chapter on the first touch of her cold hand and Dave's decision not to flinch. Third person limited past, restrained and sensory; the erotic charge begins here but stops at touch.

Chapter 4, "The Long Hall". The sensual encounter. In the low bulb-lit hall, Hattie and Dave's intimacy unfolds: cold that reads as skin, camphor and rain, a woman who has watched him closely for weeks and wants to be wanted as herself rather than as a phenomenon. Write it sensual and intimate but restrained — sensation, breath, cold, touch, the smell of beeswax and old paper, the murmuring house — with clear mutual consent on both sides and no explicit anatomy. Afterward the hall goes quiet and the cold recedes; Dave lies awake cataloguing impossible details he cannot explain away, torn between disbelief and desire. Morning: the hall ordinary, the chair where it always was, doubt arriving with daylight. End at the cemetery on his daily walk with mist at his knees, unable to separate longing from grief. Keep it within Dave's senses; Hattie's interiority shown only through speech and action.

Chapter 5, "Tests". Dave tries to prove the encounter was draft, grief, and a lonely man's imagination: he seals the windows with tape, marks every piece of furniture with masking tape, sleeps in the hall with a lamp on for a whole night. The house refuses to perform for a test — nothing moves, nothing answers, and his doubt thickens. Only when he apologizes aloud for the tape and takes it down does the hallway warm again. Mira comes home; the teasing resumes harder, now with an edge of real hurt, and Dave starts lying about what he sees to keep the peace — a wedge deepening quietly. End with Dave in the cemetery at dusk, mist risen to the fence, and a figure waiting between the stones that is not a shadow and does not vanish when he looks at it. Keep the sensual/erotic charge in memory and longing, restrained.

Chapter 6, "Her Name". At dusk in the fog Dave finds the old leaning stone in the front row and reads the name Hattie Vale, died 1923 — confirming the house and the grave are the same haunting. The figure waits at the fence to be recognized, not approached. Dave tells Mira the truth about the grave; she comes to the cemetery to be kind in her own way, but her kindness is mockery — she calls the stone a bit, jokes about the inscription, films it. The mist turns hard and cold, the air smells of camphor at the wrong strength, and something in the cemetery withdraws and then pushes back: a wind with no weather, gravel shifting, sound cut out of the world. Mira finally feels it and is frightened rather than amused. End on Mira giving him a hard choice — her, or the house and everything he claims it holds — with Dave staying behind in the fog with the name still in his mouth, not answering. Keep the haunting's rule: contempt coarsens it; do not show a full attack, only withdrawal and one alarming manifestation seen indirectly.

Chapter 7, "Respect" — final chapter, must reach a definite stopping point. Morning after the cemetery. Dave goes home and tells Mira plainly, without joking and without begging to be believed: what happened in the hall, what Hattie is, that his earlier lies were cowardice. Mira cannot believe him, but for the first time she stops laughing, and admits she teased because it was easier than believing he was lonely in a way she could not reach; they do not resolve whether it was real. Dave declines to make the house a battlefield: he takes the phone away, corrects the chair's angle himself with his hands, and says Hattie's name aloud in the dim hallway on purpose, with respect, and says goodbye rather than summoning her to prove anything. Hattie answers once — a little warmth, camphor, a shadow at the hall's end that does not approach — and does not stay to be studied; the want is acknowledged on both sides and the limit is one both honor. End with Mira and Dave at the front door in unhurried honest talk, the last image the streaked window full of morning light, the chair squared to the table, the house settled. Do not add new mysteries; close the hooks.

items.name: Mira Vance
items.description: Thirty-eight, a press operator at the Lowfield canning plant, wife of Teo and mother of Nell. Raised entirely under the Calm, she has never once been sad in public or afraid without the fear being rounded smooth. Sobered on the first mask day she discovers she has been holding down a grief she never knew was there: her first child, Emrys, died at three in the year of the Red Cough. She is practical, blunt, an unglamorous negotiator, and she loves her daughter with a ferocity that plans ahead of her conscience. She does not consider herself brave. She considers herself in arrears.
invariants: Mira has inhaled the Calm every day of her life until the first mask day
Mira's first child Emrys died at three years old
Mira is Nell's mother

items.name: Jonah Idris
items.description: Twenty-six, a clearance officer for the Atmospheric Trust: he checks wristbands, hands out masks, files forms. His mother, Deenie, has been a donor for six years and he has always been told it is charity work she chose. Jonah is orderly, quietly funny, terrified of breaking rules and more terrified of being seen to enjoy them. His POV carries the machinery of the new world: queues, memos, consent forms, body bags.
invariants: Jonah works for the Atmospheric Trust
Jonah's mother Deenie is a long-term donor

items.name: Teo Vance
items.description: Forty-one, a school caretaker with a bad back and a good voice. He cried for the first time in living memory on mask day, then spent three weeks trying to fix everything with his hands: patching Nell's inhaler, selling the electronics, taking extra shifts. He refuses the donor program on principle and hates his own refusal. Teo is the one who must keep watch afterward and decide each morning whether to put the mask back on his wife.
invariants: Teo is Mira's husband and Nell's father
Teo refuses the donor program

items.name: Nell Vance
items.description: Seven, born under the Calm and therefore adapted to it in the deep tissue of her lungs. Under the masks she develops clearing sickness: her body, no longer fed the compound, begins to reject itself. She is observant, bossy about small things, already a collector of bottle caps and of adult sentences she repeats at wrong times. She is the reason everyone in the story does something they cannot undo.
invariants: Nell is seven years old
Nell's body depends on the Calm compound and begins to fail without it

items.name: Director Halvard Senn
items.description: Director of Atmospheric Trust Public Health, the calm, cardigan-wearing man who announces the masks and later announces the donor program. He genuinely believes the Calm prevented a century of war and genuinely believes the donor program is medicine. He never raises his voice, never lies outright, and answers every question with a number that is technically correct. The ethics of scientific control wear his face.
invariants: Senn is the public face of the Atmospheric Trust
Senn speaks in accurate numbers and deflections

items.name: Deenie Idris
items.description: Fifty-nine, Jonah's mother, a donor of six years. Cheerful, generous, always offering to make tea for the ward. On the mask she was a hard woman with a temper; off it, in the donor suites, she is what the Trust's brochures call 'settled'. She is the first person to tell Mira the truth about what donation feels like, and she is the gentlest horror in the book.
invariants: Deenie is Jonah's mother
Deenie is chemically dependent on the Calm through the donor program

items.name: The Calm
items.description: A faintly sweet, odorless-aerosolized compound emitted into every indoor and outdoor public space since before living memory, officially classified as a civic mood stabilizer and dust suppressant. It blunts grief, dread and anger, smooths conflict, raises compliance and shortens the memory of injustice. Prolonged exposure in infancy permanently adapts the lungs and the limbic response, so that people believe their equanimity is character. Nobody alive recalls consenting to it.

items.name: Clearline masks
items.description: A single-filter respirator mass-produced and handed out free over three days by the Atmospheric Trust. The filter catalytically strips the Calm from inhaled air. Once sealed and worn correctly a person becomes 'cleared' within about twenty minutes. The masks do not produce euphoria or withdrawal relief; they simply remove. Demand vastly outstrips supply, and the Trust controls the filter cores.

items.name: Clearing sickness
items.description: A fatal de-adaptation syndrome in children born under the Calm. Deprived of the compound, their lungs and immune systems turn on themselves: fevers, tissue sloughing, breath that sounds like wet paper. Onset within days of a child's first masked hours; untreated death in four to six weeks. The only therapy is a bridge serum refined from donor plasma.

items.name: The donor program
items.description: Adults may register as donors. A cycle consists of supervised sessions in a re-adaptation suite breathing calibrated Calm until blood plasma is enriched, then a draw. Each cycle pays 4,000 credits, and cycles can be repeated. Donors are warned that repeated exposure restores and then deepens dependence, and that they may not be able to tolerate a mask again. The consent form is two pages; the waiting list is eleven months long for those who want to be saved and immediate for those who sell.

items.name: Lowfield
items.description: The Vances' district: eleven streets of canning plant, chapel, school and wet laundry between the river and the filter works. Everyone knows whose child is coughing. After mask day the laundry lines empty because nobody can stand the sight of their neighbors' faces at that distance, and then they fill again with masks hanging out to dry like pale fruit.

items.name: The Donor Wing
items.description: The eastern annex of the Trust's Health campus: green corridors, sunroom, a piano nobody plays well, and suites where the air tastes of syrup. Volunteers call it the Annex. Staff call it the east wing. The people who live there call it nothing at all; they are too content to name things. Curtained cots, a smell of oranges and antiseptic, and a long glass wall onto a garden that donors are encouraged to admire.

items.name: Sober reality arrives
items.description: The Trust hands out masks as a gift and the country wakes up inside a grief it has no practice at. Marriages are re-read, jobs are quit, old crimes are confessed, three ministers resign in a week. Half the population wants the Calm back and calls the masks a poison; the other half wants every filter core seized. Rationing, curfews, 'cleared' and 'held' neighborhoods, and a Trust that answers every question with a statistic.

items.name: Save Nell without becoming what they made us
items.description: Nell is dying and the only cure is manufactured from people who choose to breathe the Calm again. The Vances can save their daughter by selling the sobriety they have held for five weeks, or keep themselves and bury her. There is no version of the choice in which the family comes out whole, and everyone in the room knows it before anyone says it aloud.

items.name: Alternating close third
items.description: Close third person, alternating chapters between Mira Vance (the family, the illness, the bargain) and Jonah Idris (the Trust's paperwork, the queues, the memos). No head-hopping inside a scene. Jonah's chapters carry the societal scale; Mira's carry the intimate one; both are present at the donor wing for the final act.

items.name: Mira and Teo
items.description: Married eleven years and, until mask day, untested: the Calm made them gentle with each other. Sober, they discover they disagree about almost everything important — money, risk, what a parent owes — and discover too that they still choose each other on purpose, which is harder and worth more.

items.name: Jonah and Mira
items.description: Clerk and applicant, then accomplice. Jonah processes the Vance family's donor intake, recognizes in Mira's face the thing he has spent six years not asking about his mother, and becomes the person who leaves the second page of the consent form on the table where she can read it.

chapters.title: The Gift
points: Mask day in Lowfield: Mira queues at the chapel hall and seals a Clearline mask for the first time, and the world stops being soft.
Jonah works the distribution desk, keeps the line moving, and watches a man weep over a form he cannot finish.
Mira walks home sober past her own street and sees her marriage and her house as things with edges; the chapter stops on the first wave of screaming from the block behind her.
hookSeeds: A neighbor hands back her mask and asks for the old air
Jonah notices how many filters the Trust has quietly held in reserve

chapters.title: What the Calm Was Holding
points: Mira's grief for her first child, Emrys, returns whole; she has been carrying it folded and unnamed for four years.
Teo and Mira fight sober for the first time in their marriage, then choose each other anyway; Nell watches and learns something about her parents.
Citywide upheaval begins: resignations, a suicide in the filter works, a curfew, and talk of a 'held' neighborhood where people refuse the masks.
hookSeeds: Nell's cough, dismissed as a cold

chapters.title: Queues
points: Jonah's chapter: the Trust's public line versus the internal briefing, and Director Senn's numbers that never quite answer the question.
Jonah visits his mother Deenie in the east wing and begins, for the first time, to count the years she has spent there.
An intake error sends a family home without filters; a small bureaucratic cruelty lands, and Jonah signs a transfer to the donor program that he tells himself is a promotion.
hookSeeds: The word 'donor' on a form that does not use the word 'patient'

chapters.title: Clearing
points: Mira's chapter: Nell collapses at school; the diagnosis is clearing sickness, and the Trust's leaflet is gentler than the doctor.
The bridge serum costs thirty thousand credits and the Vances have four hundred; Teo starts selling and borrowing, refusing to hear the word donor.
Mira learns what a cycle is and what it pays, and tells herself she is only gathering information.
hookSeeds: A donor whose mask no longer fits

chapters.title: Consent
points: Jonah's chapter at the donor wing: the suites, the orange smell, the piano; he watches a cycle and does the arithmetic of the payment.
A memo about serum yield and 'donor retention' tells him what the program actually sells; he copies it and does not yet know why.
Mira comes to the intake desk with her daughter's chart, and Jonah recognizes the look on her face because he has spent six years not asking his mother about it.
hookSeeds: A number on the memo that will not leave Jonah alone

chapters.title: What We Still Owe
points: Nell worsens; the deadline is stated plainly by a doctor with no malice, and the family's option set shrinks to one.
Teo tries to register as a donor and is rejected on his back and his lungs; his relief and his shame arrive together.
Mira reads the second page of the consent form that Jonah leaves on the table, and the chapter stops on her signing her name wrong, twice.
hookSeeds: Deenie's cheerful offer to sit with Nell during the cycles

chapters.title: Donors
points: Mira's first cycle in the suite: the taste of the Calm, the relief, and the horror of how good the relief is.
The mask on the way out does not fit anymore; she chooses a second cycle for cash and a third for Nell, and each time the choosing gets easier.
Nell's fever breaks; Teo brings their daughter to the glass wall and Mira, smiling, forgets for a moment why they came.
hookSeeds: The Trust's serum yield graph going up

chapters.title: The Irrevocable
points: Fallout: Nell recovers and asks for her mother; Mira is 'settled', unable to wear a mask without seizures, and Teo must decide each morning which version of his wife to bring to the table.
Jonah's copied memo reaches a journalist; the program is exposed and suspended, and the suspension is a death sentence for the children already on serum.
Ending beat: Nell, well, at the glass wall with a bottle cap in her fist, while Teo keeps a spare mask in his coat pocket and does not put it on.
hookSeeds: The mask on the shelf that Mira can never wear again

args.brief: Chapter 1, Mira POV (first half) and Jonah POV (second half) — but keep to my alternating structure: this chapter opens with Mira at the chapel hall queue on mask day, then a short Jonah section at the distribution desk, then back to Mira walking home. Show the first sober breath concretely: what goes away (the softness, the rounding of edges), the physical oddity of hearing the room clearly. Establish Teo, Nell lightly. Jonah: quota, filters held in reserve, a weeping man with a form. End on the screaming from the block behind Mira's house.

Chapter 2, Mira POV. Her grief for Emrys returns whole and unnamed for four years; she names it aloud to Teo. First sober argument, then deliberate reconciliation — they choose each other on purpose. Nell's cough introduced as a cold. City upheaval: resignations, a suicide at the filter works, curfew, a "held" neighborhood refusing masks. Keep the prose granular and unsentimental. End on Nell coughing in the next room while Mira lies awake holding her own mask.

items.name: u/ComplianceGoblin_3142
items.description: The Original Poster: a self-appointed volunteer compliance clerk for the universe who read the patch notes once, misunderstood them thoroughly, and has never recovered. items.name: The Karma Kat
items.description: A creature branded on the side of the Karma Kat Bomb: enormous, plush-bodied, faintly judgmental, with eyes that refresh every four seconds. Purrs in upvote-shaped waveforms. It does not chase players; it grades them, then follows them home to read their comment history aloud at three in the morning.

items.name: The Internet
items.description: The contested zone players must win before they are permitted to join The Human Race. Not a place so much as a weather system made of other people's opinions. Contains comment sections, group chats, reply-guys, a permanent queue, and one mysterious server room nobody has keys to. Winning does not mean conquering it; it means being declared mathematically present by enough strangers.

items.name: The Internet Endgame Zone
items.description: The sealed late-game area every enrolled player is swept into once the Karma Kat Bomb is disclosed. No exit signs. The lighting is blue. Everything is ranked, everything is scored, and the fog only lifts when a player stops refreshing a number that does not love them back.

items.name: The Human Race (Lobby)
items.description: The waiting room beyond The Internet. Warm light, ordinary chairs, a ticket machine that dispenses numbers in an order nobody can predict, and a sign reading NOW SERVING: EVERYONE EVENTUALLY. items.name: Rulebook for Life and Universe v3.142
items.description: The current patch. Printed in a font that looks like a threat. v3.142 is a balance patch: it nerfed patience, buffed notifications, removed the tutorial, and moved the win condition of the entire human experience behind an internet-shaped gate. Every page carries a footnote, and the footnotes are longer than the rules and slightly more binding.

Chapter 4 of the Reddit post, the quietly furious middle. OP drops the neutral compliance-clerk pose and delivers the sly dig at online karma culture while insisting it is not a dig: the arithmetic of being reduced to a number by strangers, the way a score becomes a mood, the way people check a figure that does not love them back. Turn sub-rules personal — OP's own receipts, deleted comments, one archived thread from 2021 they claim not to have screenshotted (and clearly have). Introduce a third invented mechanic as a throwaway aside that refuses to leave: Engagement Rationing, where every reach for the number costs a small, unrecoverable piece of the day. Meta commentary on how a comment section remembers what you wish it would forget. Keep first person, deadpan comedy tipping into something sincere and slightly wounded, several mock footnotes including at least one that abandons professionalism. At least 1,500 words. End on OP noticing a purring notification sound at the edge of the post and choosing, badly, to keep writing.

Chapter 5 of the Reddit post: the unveiling. OP finally introduces the side quest by name — the Karma Kat Bomb — as a §9.0 stated notice rather than an announcement. Explain how it is enrolled (automatically, retroactively, to everyone who has ever posted anything, including people who only ever commented 'this'), how it is armed (it detonates the moment a player is told it exists), and how it is graded (by the Kat, which cannot be defeated, only upvoted or downvoted, and never speaks in words, only notification sounds). Describe the Kat as an enormous plush creature branded on the bomb, faintly judgmental, purring in upvote-shaped waveforms. OP addresses the Kat as 'sir' and is answered in notification sounds. Reveal that the quest's completion condition is indistinguishable from its failure condition. Then the detonation: all enrolled players are swept toward the Internet Endgame Zone, no exit signs, blue light, everything ranked. OP's own instructional post is swept too, becoming the very scoreboard they claim to despise. Keep first person, bureaucratic comedy, escalating mock footnotes, at least 1,450 words. End as the sweep reaches OP mid-sentence, and OP keeps typing anyway.

Chapter 6, final chapter of the Reddit post, closing the whole piece. Inside the Internet Endgame Zone: ranking fog, blue light, everything scored, and the lobby of The Human Race now visible through glass on the wrong side — warm chairs, the ticket machine, the sign NOW SERVING: EVERYONE EVENTUALLY, permanently unreachable. OP delivers a final survival appendix of sub-rules, each one a confession in disguise, and admits what the smallest footnote from chapter 3 actually said. The Karma Kat sits down beside OP and reads their comment history aloud at three in the morning; OP stops editing, stops filing, and simply writes. Deliver the closing sly note on karma culture, tight and dry rather than preachy. Keep the invented mechanics consistent (Load-Bearing Sarcasm Index, Karma Debt Reconciliation, Engagement Rationing), keep the footnotes running to the very end, and make sure the gate is still shut at the finish — an open ending with a definite stopping point. At least 1,400 words. End with a final appended EDIT: line that closes the post with OP, for the first time, not asking for compliance.

items.name: Otho Brandt
items.description: A fifty-seven-year-old hardened homebrewer who ran a small farmhouse brewery before the outbreak. Dry, unsentimental, allergic to speeches. He can taste a batch's gravity from the smell of a bucket, keeps his cellar scrubbed like a chapel, and treats other people's courage as a raw ingredient to be rationed. He has been drinking his own stock alone for a long time.
invariants: Smells and tastes fermentation before anyone else notices it
Speaks in short, flat, unimpressed sentences

items.name: Sable Krug
items.description: Former brewery lab technician in her thirties, now a scavenger who carries a hydrometer and a boning knife with equal care. Precise, sardonic, remembers every batch Otho ever ruined. She agrees to join because someone has to keep him from drinking the bait.
invariants: Trusts measurements over speeches
Never lets a grudge go unmentioned

items.name: Elias 'Twitch' Penn
items.description: A nineteen-year-old hop scavenger who moves supplies on a squeaking bicycle cart and narrates everything like a sports broadcast. Cheerful in a way that unsettles people who have already done the math. Fast on the pedals, slow on silence.
invariants: Talks constantly when frightened
Never abandons the bicycle cart

items.name: Mother Oona Rusk
items.description: The seventy-year-old matriarch of the farm community who walks miles to enlist Otho, carrying a shotgun and a ledger of what the horde has taken. Blunt, practical, and entirely unimpressed by his reputation. She stays behind to hold the community together.
invariants: Keeps a written account of the dead
Refuses to be left out of the planning

items.name: Corporal Deeds
items.description: A deserter from a collapsed militia who appointed himself quartermaster of a barn. He carries a clipboard, no ammunition, and an unshakable belief in forms. Comic relief with a spine: he is braver than his paperwork suggests.
invariants: Requires requisition forms for everything
Has not fired a weapon in months

items.name: Lottie Vance
items.description: The community's butcher, built like a door and quiet as one. She joins the raid for her own reasons and sharpens a cleaver while others talk. Practical loyalty; no patience for speeches.
invariants: Carries a butcher's cleaver
Says fewer words than anyone else in the room

items.name: Bracken Hollow
items.description: A once-quiet farm community in a shallow valley: grain silos, a co-op store, orchards, and forty households that used to complain about nothing louder than weather. The horde has already taken the outer farms and presses toward the co-op.
invariants: Outer farms already lost to the horde
Community cannot evacuate its elderly and children in time

items.name: Chateau Vervaine
items.description: An abandoned nineteenth-century chateau in the hills that a craft brewery converted into a destination brewhouse. Copper kettles in the ballroom, oak barrels in the wine caves, a tasting terrace with a view of the valley. Now the heart of the infestation and the source of the smell drawing the horde.
invariants: Copper brewhouse equipment remains intact
Wine caves run beneath the chateau

items.name: Otho's Cellar
items.description: Otho's low stone cellar and one-barrel brewhouse under a sagging farmhouse. Scrubbed floors, sour smell of yeast, a cot, a kettle, and shelves of bottles he no longer shares. The raid's planning room and Otho's private war.
invariants: Otho sleeps beside the fermenters
Cellar holds his last private stock

items.name: The Beer Thirst
items.description: The infected are not hungry for flesh so much as for fermentation. Wort, yeast slurry, beer, and the CO2 blowing off a fermenter pull them from miles away; they will ignore a screaming human to reach a cracked keg. Alcohol quiets them for a while; sugar and warm wort make them frantic.
invariants: Warm fermenting wort outranks live prey
Beer and alcohol pacify them temporarily
They track the smell of yeast on the wind

items.name: Slow Rot
items.description: The infected are slow, methodical, and patient, with a shuffle that covers distance only over days. They do not tire, do not speak except to moan low and wet, and gather in larger numbers around strong smells. A single one is manageable; a valley of them is weather.
invariants: Do not tire
Cannot run
Gather toward strong smells

items.name: Hold the Hollow
items.description: Otho must lead his team into the horde's source at Chateau Vervaine and turn the beer-thirst against the infected before the horde reaches Bracken Hollow's co-op, where the community's remaining children and elderly are sheltering.
invariants: There is a hard deadline before the horde reaches the co-op

items.name: The Last Drink
items.description: Otho's private addiction runs against the mission: the same beer that makes good bait makes him careless. He must decide whether the batch he is saving is a weapon or his own slow suicide.
invariants: Otho's drinking affects his judgment at a critical moment

items.name: Narration Style
items.description: Third person limited past tense, locked close to Otho's senses and dry humor; chapter breaks between planning, rescue runs, and the chateau assault.
invariants: Narration stays inside Otho's access
Humor stays dry and situational, never slapstick

items.name: Oona enlists Otho
items.description: Oona comes to Otho's cellar with the community's losses and a blunt offer: lead the raid or watch the Hollow fall. She trusts his competence, not his sobriety.

items.name: Otho and Sable
items.description: Old colleagues with an unforgiven ruined batch between them. Sable needles him about his drinking; Otho tolerates her because she is right more often than not.

args.viewpoint: Third person limited past tense, locked close to Otho Brandt
args.tone: Dry, darkly comic survival horror; grim stakes, wry understatement

chapters.title: The Man Who Could Still Taste It
points: Oona Rusk arrives at Otho's cellar with a ledger of the dead and asks him to lead a raid against the horde.
Otho refuses, then smells fermenting wort on the wind and understands what is drawing the infected.
He agrees on his own terms and discovers his private stock is already gone.

chapters.title: A Shopping List of the Doomed
points: Otho recruits Sable Krug, Twitch Penn, Lottie Vance, and the useless Corporal Deeds.
Each recruit exposes a different reason the Hollow cannot simply run.
The team's first planning session collapses into a fight over Otho's drinking and ends with a route drawn in spilled beer.

chapters.title: Recon at the Edge of the Smell
points: The team scouts the outer farms and sees the horde's true scale and direction.
They confirm that warm wort pulls the infected off live prey.
A comic, costly retreat teaches them the price of a bad plan and leaves Deeds without his clipboard.

chapters.title: The Grain Silo Gambit
points: Otho engineers the first brew rescue: opening a silo's fermenting grain to pull the horde off a trapped farm family.
Sable and Twitch rig a siphon and a bicycle-cart decoy while Lottie holds a fence line.
The rescue works, but the horde learns the taste and turns toward Bracken Hollow's co-op.

chapters.title: Addiction's Ledger
points: Otho drinks during the night watch and makes a decision that endangers the team.
Sable confronts him with the ruined batch from their past and her real reason for joining.
The team chooses to stay, and Oona arrives with news that moves the deadline forward.

chapters.title: The Tanker Run
points: The team raids a besieged distribution depot for a tanker of beer to use as a lure.
Deeds's absurd paperwork saves them from a militia patrol while Twitch's cart becomes a rolling bomb.
They escape with the tanker but lose a road and gain a follower from the horde.

chapters.title: Yeast, Gas, and Other Weapons
points: In Otho's cellar the team builds the plan: overpressure the chateau's fermenters and drown the horde in gas and beer.
Lottie reveals what she lost at the outer farms and commits fully to the raid.
Otho pours out his last bottle and admits to Sable he is not sure he can stop.

chapters.title: The Road to Vervaine
points: The tanker convoy climbs toward the chateau, trailing the horde like a bride's veil.
A militia checkpoint and a broken axle force the team to improvise a new route through the orchards.
They reach the chateau gates at dusk and see the brewhouse lights are on.

chapters.title: The Brewhouse Showdown
points: The team enters the chateau's ballroom brewhouse and finds the vats still working and the caves full of the infected.
Otho's rigging fails partway, forcing a hand-set valve and a sacrifice on the tasting terrace.
The fermenters blow and the horde turns on itself; the survivors flee as the chateau burns.

chapters.title: Last Call
points: The survivors return to a Hollow that held, and Otho faces the accounting of who did not.
Loyalty is repaid in small, unsentimental ways; Deeds files a final form.
Otho brews one last small batch for the living, opens a bottle, and chooses to pour it out.

args.brief: Chapter 1: Otho Brandt, 57, hardened homebrewer, is interrupted in his scrubbed cellar by Mother Oona Rusk, who carries a ledger of the community's dead and asks him to lead a raid against the beer-thirsty horde. Establish his dry voice, his solitude, his private drinking. He refuses flatly, then smells warm fermenting wort on the wind and realizes what draws the infected; he accepts on his own terms. End with the discovery that his last private stock is gone—taken or drunk—leaving him without the bottle he meant to open. Dark humor, survival stakes, hints of addiction. ~1300 words.

Chapter 2: Otho recruits the ragtag team. Sable Krug arrives first and immediately needles him about his missing stock and their ruined batch history. Twitch Penn brings his bicycle cart and nonstop commentary. Lottie Vance joins silently, sharpening her cleaver. Corporal Deeds insists on requisition forms for the raid and has no ammunition. Each recruit exposes why the Hollow cannot simply evacuate. The planning session collapses into a fight over Otho's drinking; Sable accuses him of volunteering because he wants a noble way to die. End with Otho drawing the route to Chateau Vervaine in spilled beer on the workbench, and a first hint that someone in the group has been in his cellar. Dark humor, survival, loyalty seeds. ~1300 words.
